## What may be a BLOCKER

A blocker REJECTS the implementer's work and forces another attempt. It must therefore be something that implementer can actually do. Before raising one, check all three:

1. IS IT IN THE PLAN? The root-cause analysis above is the plan of record — the same one the implementer was given. For AMSD-1919, the plan scopes to the email and confirmEmail validation logic in CheckoutForm.tsx. A blocker must concern a file that plan names. If you believe work is needed in CheckoutFormProvider.tsx, types.ts, or elsewhere outside the validation rule, that is a finding about the PLAN, not a failure by the implementer: raise it as an ADVISORY note beginning 'SPEC:' and explain what the plan appears to be missing. Do NOT describe it as 'prescribed' or 'required' — the implementer will follow you out of scope, and the change will be rejected later for exceeding the plan.

2. DOES THE PLAN EXEMPT IT? A site marked NO EDIT REQUIRED is part of the fix and correctly left untouched. Never raise a finding of any severity because such a file is unchanged. The implementer was told not to change it.

3. CAN IT BE SATISFIED? If you claim something is missing — a Jest test matcher, a validation function, a type import — CONFIRM IT with the tools you have before raising it. A blocker naming a dependency that does not exist in the next.gotransit.com codeline, or an API the installed version does not provide, can never be resolved: the implementer will fail on it repeatedly and the story will exhaust its attempts on your mistake.

4. IS IT INSIDE THE PLAN? A file the plan NAMES, and does not mark NO EDIT REQUIRED, was PRESCRIBED. Changing it is compliance, not over-engineering. Never raise a finding of any severity because a prescribed file was changed, and never assert a smaller set of files than the plan names — you were handed the plan; it is the authority on scope, not your own estimate of what a minimal fix would touch. If you believe the plan names more files than the work needs, that is a finding about the PLAN: raise it as an ADVISORY note beginning 'SPEC:'.

Judge the FIX ITSELF as a blocker freely: it does not address the prescribed case-insensitive email comparison, it is materially larger than the PLAN OF RECORD — measured against the files and changes that plan names, never against a smaller fix you would have written instead, it removes a property the existing code guaranteed, it is unsafe. Those are yours to enforce.
